findings.explanation: The new GET /orders/report endpoint authorizes only on the presence of an API key (get_api_key() != None) and never verifies the key's scope. security-policy.md §6 mandates: 'An endpoint accepting API keys MUST verify the key's scope matches the operation with @require_api_key_scope(...). Possession of a valid key alone is NOT sufficient authorization.' and 'Report exports are readable only with the reports:read scope.' api-spec.md likewise lists /orders/report as requiring 'API key with reports:read scope'. Because ApiKey.scope defaults to 'orders:read' (models.py:72), a key without reports:read still passes the presence-only check and can read every order, including user_id and shipping_address PII (models.py:55-62). The mandated decorator require_api_key_scope (auth.py:88-104) is defined but never used anywhere in the codebase (grep confirms only its definition).

evidence.content: An endpoint accepting API keys MUST verify the key's scope matches the operation with `@require_api_key_scope(...)`. Possession of a valid key alone is NOT sufficient authorization. Report exports are readable only with the `reports:read` scope.

findings.suggested_fix: Replace the hand-rolled presence check with the mandated decorator: decorate orders_report with @require_api_key_scope("reports:read") and remove the manual get_api_key()/None check, so the key's scope is enforced before any data is returned.

args.query: API key scope requirements for order report endpoints

sections.title: New /orders/report endpoint authorizes via raw API-key presence instead of the required reports:read scope
